ai.description: The Yellow Monitor reaches 1 meter in length. It is olive-brown with dark transverse bands and a distinct yellow-tinged belly. A dark temporal streak and rounded snout distinguish this species.
ai.identificationRemarks: The *Varanus flavescens* is best identified by its distinct, bright yellow-to-golden belly and throat, which lack the dark cross-bands found on other Indian monitor species.
ai.habitat: The Yellow Monitor inhabits lowland riverine forests, marshes, and agricultural fields in the Indian subcontinent, typically found at elevations below 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The yellow monitor is primarily diurnal and semi-aquatic, frequently foraging along riverbanks and marshes for small vertebrates, insects, and crustaceans.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Varanus flavescens* is oviparous, laying a single clutch of 15–30 eggs annually. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between July and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Varanus flavescens* inhabits the Indo-Gangetic plains and Himalayan foothills, ranging from Pakistan through northern India to Bangladesh, typically below 1,500 meters.
